outputs.L1: The electroluminescence device according to the disclosure includes: a base material having a recessed portion; a light-emitting element including a reflective layer provided on a front surface of the recessed portion, an optically transparent filling layer that fills the recessed portion with the reflective layer interposed therebetween, an optically transparent first electrode provided on the filling layer, an organic layer including a light-emitting layer provided on the first electrode, and an optically transparent second electrode provided on the organic layer; and an active element connected to the light-emitting element. A display region includes a plurality of unit regions separated from one another, each unit region including a plurality of the light-emitting elements and active elements configured to control light emission from the plurality of light-emitting elements. The reflective layer of at least one of the light-emitting elements provided in the plurality of recessed portions functions as a contact portion with the active element.
outputs.L2: The disclosed electroluminescent device comprises a substrate having recessed portions and light-emitting elements disposed therein. Each light-emitting element includes a reflective layer formed on the front surface of a corresponding recessed portion; an optically transparent filling layer that fills the recessed portion over the reflective layer; an optically transparent first electrode arranged on the filling layer; an organic layer, including a light-emitting layer, disposed on the first electrode; and an optically transparent second electrode formed on the organic layer. The device further comprises active elements electrically connected to the light-emitting elements. Its display region is partitioned into multiple separate unit regions, each of which contains a plurality of light-emitting elements and active elements configured to regulate light emission from those light-emitting elements. In at least one of the light-emitting elements provided in the plurality of recessed portions, the reflective layer also serves as a contact portion for connection to an active element.
outputs.L3:
The electroluminescence device includes a base material provided with a plurality of recessed portions, each of which contains a light-emitting element. Each light-emitting element comprises a reflective layer disposed within the recessed portion, a transparent filling layer, a transparent first electrode, an organic light-emitting layer, and a transparent second electrode. The reflective layer redirects emitted light toward the viewing side of the device, while the transparent layers permit the light to pass through.

Active elements are electrically connected to the light-emitting elements and selectively control their light emission. The display region of the device is divided into multiple unit regions, with each unit region containing a plurality of light-emitting elements and their corresponding active elements. In at least one of the recessed portions, the reflective layer additionally serves as a contact portion that electrically connects the associated light-emitting element to its active element. This dual-purpose configuration can simplify the device structure and improve the efficient use of space within the display region.
outputs.L4:
An electroluminescence device includes a substrate divided into a plurality of display regions, each of which may contain one or more light-emitting elements and associated active control elements. Recessed portions are formed within the display regions and are filled with a transparent material to provide an optical path and a substantially planar surface for the overlying device structures. Reflective layers are arranged in relation to the recessed portions so that light generated by the light-emitting elements is redirected toward a desired viewing surface, thereby improving light extraction and display efficiency.

Each light-emitting element includes a transparent electrode, one or more organic electroluminescent layers, and an opposing electrode arranged in a layered configuration. The organic layers emit light when an electric field is applied between the electrodes. The active control elements, which may include thin-film transistors or other switching and driving components, selectively supply current to the corresponding light-emitting elements. At least one of the reflective layers additionally functions as an electrical contact or interconnection and is electrically coupled to an active control element. By allowing the reflective structure to perform both optical and electrical functions, the device reduces the space required for separate contacts and wiring. This arrangement enables compact integration of the emission structures and control circuitry within the divided display regions while maintaining efficient optical performance and reliable electrical operation.

### The Power of “The”

“The” is one of the smallest yet most frequently used words in the English language. Known as the definite article, it identifies a particular person, place, object, or idea. For example, “a book” can mean any book, while “the book” refers to a specific one.

Although it may seem insignificant, “the” brings clarity and precision to communication. It helps readers and listeners understand what is already known, unique, or important in a sentence. This simple word demonstrates how even the smallest elements of language can have a powerful role in shaping meaning.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an electroluminescent display structure where a display region is divided into unit regions, each having multiple recessed light emitters and corresponding control circuitry, with one reflective layer doubling as a contact to an active element.
counterfactuals.output:
An electroluminescent display includes a substrate whose display area is partitioned into a plurality of unit regions, such as pixels. Each unit region contains multiple recessed portions, with an electroluminescent light-emitting element formed in each recess. Control circuitry, including an active element such as a thin-film transistor, is provided for selectively driving the corresponding emitters.

A reflective conductive layer is formed beneath or along the recessed emitters to reflect light toward the viewing side. The same layer extends to the control circuitry and directly functions as an electrode contact—such as a source or drain contact—of the active element. Thus, one conductive layer performs both optical reflection and electrical interconnection, reducing layer count and simplifying fabrication.
